detail.longDescription:
So, I have no idea what I'm doing, but I had this old HP zBook lying around (the thing is from 2014 I think?) with 32gb of RAM and a 1tb SSD in it, just doing nothing.

So I installed linux mint and was like... ok, now what? It's too heavy and awkward to use as a daily-use laptop. 

Then I remembered NextCloud and was like - yeah, I wonder if I could host my own NextCloud and use this machine instead of Google Docs/Google Drive? And NextCloud can do a bunch of other stuff too...

So I found two other 1tb thunderbolt drives that I wasn't actually using, and plugged those in. I also already had a non-managed 2.5gb ethernet switch for my work computer's connection (it needs to be ethernet - I need the speed)...

So now I have a pretty respectable hardware setup.... but no idea how to get it all to work.

I know, I know, I could just go to the Linux Mint forums and ask people for step-by-step instructions (which I feel like could be a disaster for me). Or I could read a book. Or I could do any number of things that would take me infinite hours to learn and comprehend and understand.

So what do I do? Yeah, I did it. I asked duck.ai how to do it. And you know what? I'm 90% of the way there after probably a grand total of two hours or so of "work" off/on between actual real work jobs. 

So far the hardest part has been trying to get the thing to not go to sleep when I shut the lid.

Anyway, obviously if I want help from an ai, I should at least be using a local AI setup - and that will come eventually. But I'm learning so much. And I'm not annoying the guys on the forums.

And this is actually making it fun. It's like I have a very patient older brother just walking me through each step. I never had an older brother. This is kinda nice, honestly.

Anyway, I'm just saying there is a place for AI, and it's for stuff like this. At least it is for me.

Thanks for coming to my ted talk.

#linux #linuxmint #nextcloud #homeserver #selfhosted #selfhosting #newbie #ai #duckDuckFedi
